reading.body:
Flexential Atlanta—Douglasville 2 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, the largest declared single facility footprint in Georgia, and alone represents 86 percent of the state's published megawatt capacity among mapped data centers.

The 358,000 square feet of technical space can support between 900 and 3,600 racks depending on workload density. At 40 kW per rack, a density associated with AI training, the facility holds roughly 900 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical for colocation, it scales to 3,600. The operator has not disclosed which density applies, so actual rack count remains an assumption tied to tenant workload mix.

The certification stack—HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, and SSAE 18—qualifies the facility to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, payments, and defense applications. ITAR clearance in particular narrows the field of eligible operators and admits tenants handling controlled technical data for defense purposes. No certification directly enables or restricts AI compute.

Georgia has 33 mapped facilities on this site. Only two publish a megawatt figure. This published scarcity reflects the difficulty of extracting capacity data from operator websites rather than true distribution, meaning the real concentration of Georgia capacity across available facilities remains unknown.
